report:
PASS for the explicitly scoped sufficient-condition answer A–F. The argument establishes an intrinsic countable divisorial-order criterion on P² with a positive pluriclosed background and strictly positive smooth residual. It computes both extremal singularity volumes by proving the mass formula for every representative of the resulting ordinary type. It answers a restricted portion of P06’s positivity programme; it settles no previously unresolved zero-lower-volume implication and gives no unrestricted classification or modification mass law.

A. The normalization and countable passage are valid. For a unit linear section, x=|s(Z)|²/||Z||² has density 2(1−x) on [0,1] under κ², so its logarithmic mean is −3/2. Consequently ∫|u₀|κ²=3A/2. The decreasing series therefore defines a genuine, nontrivial quasi-psh potential, and Poincaré–Lelong gives dd^c u=S−Aκ. Since θ+dd^c u=R+S and R>0, admissibility and strict bigness follow directly.

On each fixed smooth compact modification, the canonical pulled-back tail is nontrivial because it is finite somewhere on the biholomorphic locus. Its current T_K is closed and positive. Gauduchon’s Theorem 2 applies to that compact surface without an even-Betti or projectivity assumption. Subtracting its generic E-coefficient and integrating against η gives ν_E(r_K∘π)≤C_E A_K. Finite additivity followed by A_K→0 proves convergence and the exact asserted profile. This argument does not restrict u to E. It therefore remains valid when a divisor belongs to the actual pole set despite having zero generic coefficient.

BMP is established independently: for Cκ≥h, bounded h-psh f satisfies 0≤h+dd^c f≤Cκ+dd^c f. Positivity and bounded-product multilinearity give the corresponding squared-measure inequality. The closed Bedford–Taylor recursion and distributional Stokes give total mass C² on the right. No positive lower mass is inferred from BMP.

B. The orders-to-ideals application has the correct scope. Both potentials belong to PSH(P²,Cκ) for sufficiently large C; this is a closed Kähler background. The hypothesis includes every projective modification and subsequent point blowup. The exceptional divisor of that blowup recovers the point Lelong number, so Darvas–Xia’s Theorem 2.13/Proposition 2.30 applies. Nothing identifies θ with a line-bundle curvature. Independently checking the underlying sources reveals that BFJ’s Theorem A originally concerns J+, with weight exp(−2tφ); strong openness supplies J+=J, and rescaling t supplies the present all-weight convention.

The converse on an arbitrary compact modification is also established. At a generic smooth point of E, write φ∘π=b log|ζ₁|²+ψ with ψ locally bounded above. Pullback integrability, including the holomorphic Jacobian of order j_E, forces ord_E(g∘π)+j_E+1>kb. Thus e_k/k≥b−(j_E+1)/k. Demailly’s Bergman construction permits every real m>0. Taking m=k/2 gives φ_m=k⁻¹logΣ|g_m,ℓ|²≥φ−O(k⁻¹), with every term in I(kφ). Finite extraction of the Bergman ideal gives e_k/k≤ν_E(φ_m∘π)≤b. Hence the printed estimate and limit are correct. Smooth additions change neither the ideals nor these coefficients.

C. Envelope preservation is valid, with one harmless clarification: explicitly include u in every finite maximum forming the Choquet sequence. Maxima preserve the profile because their point and generic Lelong numbers are the minima of the respective numbers. The resulting sequence satisfies u≤f_j≤0. On each fixed modification, its pullbacks converge almost everywhere off the exceptional set and are dominated in local L¹ by the genuine pullback of u. Their closed positive currents consequently converge weakly. Upper semicontinuity gives ν_E(q∘π)≥b(E), while q≥u gives the opposite inequality. Thus q is genuine and retains the profile.

Siu subtraction from Cκ+dd^c q removes every finite partial sum of S, and the increasing-sum limit remains positive. Accordingly q−u, interpreted distributionally, has a genuine (C−A)κ-psh representative. It is bounded above on compact P². Canonical almost-everywhere order extends the resulting inequality everywhere, including common poles. Together with q≥u, this proves q∼u. This is the supplied, already credited countable domination mechanism, independently reconstructed rather than accepted from the companion manuscript.

D. The entire ordinary-type quantifier is justified. For every genuine θ-psh w∼u, the same subtraction gives Cκ+dd^c w=S+K, where K=(C−A)κ+dd^c h and h is the canonical representative of w−u. Ordinary equivalence bounds h almost everywhere; canonical representation extends both bounds everywhere. Thus K has bounded local potentials. Its trace charges no pluripolar set, whereas S is supported on actual poles of w. The degree-one non-pluripolar current is therefore exactly K, even if the pole set contains additional points or divisors.

The closed top mass of u is squeezed between (C−A)² and (C−A_N)². The upper bound follows from comparison with the finite logarithmic sums using closed mass monotonicity. The lower bound follows from positive non-pluripolar multilinearity applied to S+(C−A)κ. Letting N increase proves equality. Applying closed monotonicity in both ordinary-order directions then gives ∫⟨(Cκ+dd^c w)²⟩=(C−A)² for every w∼u. No nonclosed monotonicity is invoked.

For L=Cκ−θ, use the same truncation max(w,−j) in both backgrounds and restrict the bounded expansion to {w>−j}. The closed degree-two and degree-one restrictions converge to finite non-pluripolar products; multiplication by smooth L preserves convergence, and smooth L² charges no pole set. This establishes MA_ext,θ(w)=⟨T²⟩−2L∧K+L² as finite Borel measures. Since dd^c L=0, distributional Stokes gives ∫L∧K=(C−A)∫L∧κ. Integration yields ∫MA_ext,θ(w)=∫(θ−Aκ)²>0. This proves the formula throughout the ordinary type and hence proves equality of its infimum and supremum, rather than substituting one envelope’s raw mass for either volume.

E–F. The example’s differential calculation is correct: τ is real, ∂bar∂τ=0, and where χ=1 its exterior derivative is dz₂∧dbar z₂∧(dz₁−dbar z₁), which is nonzero. Compactness permits ε>0 with θ≥κ/2, hence R≥κ/4 and ∫R²≥1/16. The Vandermonde determinant excludes any single pencil. Infinitely many positive base-divisor coefficients exclude an ideal-equivalent analytic type: an analytic type on a compact base has only finitely many prime divisorial components, and B would force it to have all the prescribed coefficients. Smooth gauge transport is a bijection of the specified ordinary types; it preserves the current, canonical poles, ideals and corrected measure. Its preservation of both extremal volumes follows from that bijection. No zero-obstacle projection identity is asserted.

Source corrections and supporting-proof boundaries are material to an accurate review. Darvas–Xia’s printed Proposition 2.14 has a factor-of-two numerical error under its stated conventions: for φ=c log|z₁|², its growth-normalized Lelong number is 2c, whereas k⁻¹ord I(kφ) tends to c. The equality characterization used here survives this common normalization, and the article supplies the correctly normalized independent local estimate. In Witt Nyström’s v1 product calculation, ordinary exterior powers require the factor binomial(n+N,N) in the moment formula. That common positive factor cancels in the comparison. After bounded decreasing approximation and plurifine exhaustion, the remaining probability kernels N t^(N−1) concentrate at t=1; closed multilinearity makes the mass function continuous there. Thus the needed monotonicity theorem is established despite the erroneous printed product normalization. The local truncation should also be written v_C=max(v,u−C), a harmless notation correction. These erroneous source formulas are not imported as premises.

The companion global-potential proof works by partition of unity and local elliptic regularity; it requires no global dd^c lemma. Its countable domination proof works after local closed smooth corrections and passage through finite divisorial subtraction. Its bounded mass-invariance proof also checks out: polarization detects dd^c(ω^j), the power identities give the differential conditions, and bounded continuity extends the result. Exact bounded smooth approximation follows by rescaling decreasing almost-positive analytic regularizations; boundedness eliminates their analytic poles. This agrees with [Chiose’s primary theorem](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.05945). The finite residual-rigidity excerpt has unexpanded normalizer and threshold/dual references, so it is an overlap record, not an independently self-contained correctness premise. Its finite-divisor removal step is valid; none of its unexpanded conclusions is needed for A–F.

The verified contribution beyond the specified finite-divisor, analytic and single-fibration examples is the countable, nonanalytic, non-pencil family with an exact all-modification ideal profile and an explicit mass throughout its entire ordinary type in a genuinely nonclosed background. The envelope mechanism and bounded pluriclosed invariance retain their existing credit. General ideal positivity, unrestricted zero-volume implications, stretching equivalences and all-obstacle conclusions remain untouched. No priority claim follows from this audit.

passages.statement: Poincaré–Lelong: for a nonzero holomorphic function g, with dd^c=(i/(2π))∂bar∂, one has dd^c log|g|²=[div(g)]. For a holomorphic section of a smoothly metrized line bundle, the corresponding formula subtracts the metric curvature.

Gauduchon’s metric theorem: on every connected compact complex manifold of complex dimension m≥2, every Hermitian metric is conformal to a smooth positive metric η satisfying dd^c(η^(m−1))=0. In particular, every compact complex surface admits smooth η>0 with dd^cη=0.
passages.quote: Toute métrique hermitienne sur une variété presque complexe compacte de dimension 2m est conforme

passages.statement: Siu decomposition: a closed positive (1,1)-current has a unique weakly convergent divisorial part Σλ_j[D_j], with λ_j the generic current coefficients and positive closed residual current. Every finite partial divisorial sum can be subtracted while retaining positivity; their increasing limit can also be subtracted. Along a prime divisor D, the restriction of the current is λ_D[D].

On a coordinate domain, a real distribution with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable psh representative. A locally uniformly upper-bounded family of psh functions has a psh usc supremum equal to its pointwise supremum almost everywhere; Choquet’s lemma supplies a countable subfamily with the same usc supremum. These assertions apply to a common smooth closed background after adding local smooth potentials.

passages.statement: If closed positive currents T_j converge weakly to T on a coordinate domain, their point Lelong numbers satisfy ν(T,x)≥limsup_j ν(T_j,x). For a common quasi-psh background, the corresponding assertion follows after a fixed local smooth correction.

Darvas–Xia, Theorem 2.13 and Proposition 2.30: on a compact Kähler manifold, for quasi-psh potentials in a common smooth closed pseudoeffective background, equality of multiplier ideals at every positive real weight is equivalent to equality of point Lelong numbers on every smooth projective modification, and equivalently to equality of all generic divisorial Lelong numbers on those modifications. A point Lelong number equals the generic number on the exceptional divisor of its blowup. Their multiplier-ideal weight is exp(−tφ).

passages.statement: Demailly’s local Bergman approximation: for psh φ on a bounded pseudoconvex domain and every real m>0, the holomorphic Hilbert space with weight exp(−2mφ) gives φ_m=(2m)⁻¹logΣ|g_m,ℓ|² satisfying φ_m≥φ−C/m. Locally, its singularity and divisorial orders are those of a finite subcollection of the Bergman terms. Every such term belongs locally to the multiplier ideal for weight exp(−2mφ).

passages.statement: Bedford–Taylor theory: locally bounded psh potentials have positive closed mixed Hessian products, symmetric and multilinear and continuous under decreasing bounded approximation. On a strongly pseudoconvex coordinate domain, pluripolar sets have zero Bedford–Taylor outer capacity. Consequently bounded local psh mixed products, including trace measures obtained by wedging with a smooth strictly positive local factor, charge no pluripolar set.
passages.quote: retains the usual algebraic properties of the operator on smooth functions.

passages.statement: Boucksom–Guedj–Lu’s bounded-background product construction: for bounded quasi-psh potentials and smooth real (1,1)-forms, smooth-background-corrected Bedford–Taylor mixed products are symmetric, multilinear, plurifinely local, non-pluripolar and depend only on the represented currents. passages.statement: Strong openness: for a psh germ φ, with I(φ) defined by local integrability of |g|²exp(−φ), one has I(φ)=⋃_{ε>0}I((1+ε)φ). The same equality applies to quasi-psh germs because smooth additions do not change local integrability.

BEGZ, Theorem 1.16: on a compact Kähler manifold, for cohomologous tuples of closed positive (1,1)-currents T_j,T'_j with small unbounded locus, if every T_j is less singular than T'_j, the difference of the cohomology classes of their non-pluripolar mixed products is pseudoeffective. For top-degree products this implies the corresponding inequality of total masses.
